properties.description: Nickel-Copper on Carbon catalyst or material

nodes.name: NiCuCr/C impregnation reduction
nodes.procedure: 300 mg of Ketjen black was dispersed in 15 ml of ethanol in a round bottom flask, and the slurry was magnetically stirred for 30 min. 3.57 g of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 0.1488 g of Cu(NO3)2·3H2O, 0.082 g of Cr(NO3)3·9H2O, 0.0238 g of urea and 0.2078 g of citric acid monohydrate were dissolved in 3 mL of deionized water. Then, the solution was added to the carbon slurry dropwise. The obtained slurry was magnetically stirred for 10 h at room temperature and then dried at 80°C in an oven. Finally, it was placed in a furnace and calcinated at 470°C for 1 h under the atmosphere of 5% H2 and 95% Ar with a gas flow rate of 50 sccm.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCuCr/C nanoparticles have average diameter of 16 nm, uniformly distributed on carbon support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1a shows the transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image of the NiCuCr/C. The NiCuCr nanoparticles appeared with an average diameter of 16 nm...

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern shows diffraction rings assigned to (111), (200), (220), and (311) facets of Ni alloy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction pattern (SAED, the upper right insert of Fig. 1a) demonstrated the good crystallinity of the nanoparticles, and the diffraction rings were assigned to the (111), (200), (220), and (311) facets of Ni alloy.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms NiCuCr/C is Ni alloy with shoulder at ~26° from carbon support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystalline phase of NiCuCr/C was further proved to be a Ni alloy by the XRD pattern (Fig. 1b). The shoulder at ca. 26° in the XRD pattern was contributed by the carbon support.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows lattice fringe spacing of 0.18 nm assigned to (200) facet of Ni; subnanometer Cr2O3 clusters with 0.26 nm (104) spacing on rough nanoparticle surfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM, Fig. 1c) and high-resolution TEM (HRTEM, Supplementary Fig. 1) image showed clear lattice fringes, and the lattice fringe with the spacing of 0.18 nm was assigned to the (200) facet of Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping shows homogeneous Ni and Cu distribution, Cr and O enriched at nanoparticle edges confirming NiCu alloy core with surface Cr2O3 oxide clusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental mapping images illustrated that Ni and Cu distributed homogeneously in the nanoparticle, while Cr was enriched at the edge of the nanoparticle, and the O distribution almost resembled that of Cr (Fig. 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCuCr/C metal contents: Ni 57.6 wt%, Cu 3.9 wt%, Cr 1.1 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The metal contents of Ni, Cu, and Cr were measured by inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES), which was 57.6, 3.9, and 1.1 wt%, respectively (Supplementary Table 1)...

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution Ni 2p XPS: Ni/C shows Ni(0) 852.1 eV, Ni(II) 853.6/855.2 eV; NiCuCr/C, NiCu/C, NiCr/C Ni(0) peaks shift +0.8 eV; Cu 2p mainly Cu(0); Cr 2p Cr(III) 577.5/587.3 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For Ni/C, the peak at 852.1 eV was assigned to the Ni(0) species, and the peaks at 853.6 and 855.2 eV were assigned to the Ni(II) species... The Ni (0) peaks of NiCuCr/C, NiCu/C, and NiCr/C show a positive shift (+0.8 eV) compared with Ni/C...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES/EXAFS confirm metallic Ni in NiCuCr with charge transfer; Cu K-edge confirms metallic Cu with Cu-Ni scattering at 2.18 Å; Cr K-edge confirms Cr2O3-like oxidized Cr(III) structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The coordination environments of NiCuCr/C were further characterized by X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) spectra.

nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 5a shows the filled valence band spectra of Ni, NiCu, NiCr, and NiCuCr... their peak positions were 0.15, 0.40, 0.20, and 0.37 eV for Ni, NiCu, NiCr, and NiCuCr, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ATR-SEIRAS at 0 V shows NiCuCr/C has 41.0% strongly H-bonded water, higher than Ni (37.1%) and NiCu (28.6%), indicating strengthened interfacial water binding.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 5b. Ni had 37.1% of strongly H-bonded water. After the introduction of Cu, the strongly H-bonded water ratio decreased to 28.6%... When Cr was introduced as the NiCuCr, a clearly increased strongly H-bonded water ratio up to 41.0% was observed...
